title: NETBCI2026
description: A longitudinal EEG dataset of right-hand motor imagery versus rest brain-computer interface (BCI) training in 19 healthy participants, each completing 4 sessions on separate days. Participants controlled a one-dimensional cursor in a two-target box task with online visual feedback, yielding 14,431 trials recorded with a 74-channel EEG system. The dataset is distributed in BIDS format with HED event annotations and supports studies of BCI skill learning and neurofeedback.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 250 Hz from 74 passive Ag/AgCl Easycap electrodes, amplified by a MEGIN TRIUX system, referenced to the mastoids with the ground on the left scapula, and acquired with BCI2000. Each session had 6 online feedback runs of up to 32 trials. Each trial had a 1 s inter-stimulus interval followed by 5 s of target presentation with cursor feedback. The up target corresponded to sustained right-hand grasping motor imagery and the down target to rest.
